instruction: Complete the required work in FreeCAD through its command-line/Python API workflow: inspect and read the supplied engineering drawing evidence, construct the required single solid with FreeCAD API or FreeCADCmd, and export the final result. Use `/usr/lib/freecad/bin/freecadcmd-python3` for the FreeCAD command-line work in this task when working on `drawing.dxf`. Mouse-driven GUI interaction is not required. The four drawing files and the public supplement table are mandatory inputs. The drawings remain the primary source for every numeric dimension printed on them. Before modeling, inspect all views in /home/user/Desktop/drawing.svg, /home/user/Desktop/drawing.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/drawing.png, and /home/user/Desktop/drawing.pdf, and read /home/user/Desktop/supplement.csv. Interpret the orthographic views using the ISO first-angle projection convention shown by the supplied TechDraw drawing; do not mirror or rearrange views as third-angle projection. The drawings intentionally carry the numeric dimensions printed on them. The supplement table is incomplete and supplies only information omitted from the drawings, such as datum/orientation, feature semantics, missing locations, directions, depths, and connectivity. Do not use it to replace or ignore a numeric dimension printed in a drawing; if a value appears in a drawing, read it from the drawing. Do not rely on the task title or evaluator hints. Read every numeric dimension printed in the drawings from the drawings themselves. Use supplement.csv only for parameters intentionally omitted from the drawings, and combine both sources to reconstruct the geometry. Reconstruct the mechanical part named "单孔列 L 形角件". Use millimetres and use the datum/orientation supplied only where the drawing omits it. Preserve the explicit dimensions, holes, openings, steps, and connectivity described by the drawing. Export only the final valid solid as /home/user/Desktop/result.step. Use only the supplied drawings and supplement.csv as task inputs; do not use evaluator-generated artifacts or evaluator implementation files. The evaluator accepts geometrically equivalent STEP files after import; it does not require byte-identical output or a particular feature order.
